summary: Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University, where an affiliation as a special researcher is attested in 2026.

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Okada studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn, and later held positions at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College and Minobusan University.
Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from around 1955 to 1963 and subsequently worked there from around 1966 to 2006.
Yukio Hattori (1932–2007) was a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University from around 1950 to 1954 and held a post at Japan Women's University.
Yukio Kotani (born 1931) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Having studied under Hanjiro Tominaga, Kotani held a position at Rissho University from around 1970 to 2002.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held posts at Toyo University and Rissho University, serving as Rissho's president in 1968.
Yukio Yamanaka works in Indology and philosophy. Yamanaka studied at Kyoto University and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

Yuko Kamishima works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Kamishima studied at Indiana University Bloomington, the University of Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, and held posts at Waseda University (2006–2016) and Ritsumeikan University (2016).
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Matsuda studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She held associate professor and professor posts at Kyoto University.
Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Zeng earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, studying under Kirill Solonin and Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama studied at Hiroshima University and under Kenyo Mitomo.
Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies. Nakamoto studied at Ryukoku University and held a research post there in 2012.
Yumiko Ishihama (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from around 1980 to 1989 and held a post there around 1997.
Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at Fudan University by 2006. Ji served as a librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Jan was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Ma completed a PhD at Columbia University, studying under Chun-fang Yu.

Yunshan Tan (1898–1983) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at institutions including Hunan First Normal University and under teachers such as Taixu and Kshitimohan Sen, later serving as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University.
Yunxi Wang (1926–2014) was a Sinology scholar. Wang studied at Fudan University from around 1947 to 1952 and held a post there from around 1952 to 2014.

Yuri Levada (1930–2006) studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1947–1952). His career included posts at Moscow State University, the Institute of Sociology, VTSIOM, the Levada Center, and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
